    Latest Update: Organized Chaos: Bournemouth’s Possession Principles Against Nottingham – MH

    📅 28 Jan 2025 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 28.01.2025 in den Kategorien Premier League,Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • In a recent development, on Matchday 23, the two surprise teams of the Premier League faced off.
    • It has been revealed that bournemouth’s coach, Andoni Iraola, is a former player under Marcelo Bielsa at Athletic Bilbao.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 28.01.2025 in den Kategorien Premier League,Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.

    In a recent development, on Matchday 23, the two surprise teams of the Premier League faced off. Nottingham, unbeaten in their last nine matches, has impressed this season with outstanding defensive work. Bournemouth, coached by Andoni Iraola and now unbeaten in 12 games, takes a completely different tactical approach compared to most other teams. In an interview with TNT Sports, Guardiola remarked: “Today, modern football is the way Bournemouth, Newcastle, Brighton, and Liverpool play.” What exactly are these teams doing differently? Bournemouth’s approach will be analyzed in detail based on this match.

    It has been revealed that bournemouth’s coach, Andoni Iraola, is a former player under Marcelo Bielsa at Athletic Bilbao. Bielsa, widely known in the Premier League as the coach who led Leeds United to promotion, gained recognition for his style of play characterized by exceptionally high intensity in all phases of the game. According to Iraola, his own footballing philosophy has been significantly shaped by his former coach Bielsa.

    Industry observers note that in an interview with Sky, back when he was still managing Rayo Vallecano, Iraola stated: “I was very lucky to play for him (Bielsa) for two seasons as a player. I think he has another vision of football. They were two very good seasons for us, and, for me, it was a different knowledge.” He also explained: “I use a lot of exercises from Marcelo that I learned from him. I use a lot of things, especially with the ball. Offensively, his teams are very dynamic. He is willing to make all the runs to the space, he is ready to accept this kind of disorder, offensively.”.

    Iraola’s tactical concept can be described as “organized chaos.” The aim is not to implement a positional system with perfect patterns of play. Instead, the focus is on creating problems for opposing teams by generating chaos. The idea is to force the opponent into unfamiliar, uncontrolled phases of play. A particularly key concept within this is highly intense, man-oriented, hybrid attacking pressing, designed to force the opponent into quick turnovers and a fast-paced, direct game.

    According to recent reports, „It is true that we like, and we perform better, in high-tempo games. We need to run a lot. We don’t need so much control, not in every single play, but I think we have the legs, we have the willingness, to go up and down.“ – Iraola.

    In a recent development, accordingly, Iraola’s style of play could face challenges against deep-lying teams that deliberately thrive on minimal possession. These teams don’t need to engage with Bournemouth’s high-intensity game but can instead remain compact out of possession. They are not required to build up play from the back under Bournemouth’s pressing to maintain controlled possession but can focus on their own offensive transitions. This season, Nottingham has been one of the most successful teams in executing such an approach. Consequently, it was particularly intriguing to observe how Iraola’s Bournemouth would operate in possession against Nottingham’s deep block.

    Iraola describes his philosophy in possession as follows:.

    Industry observers note that “We have to prepare [positional] patterns, but we cannot just prioritise them. If you can see that you don’t have a teammate ahead, forget about the pattern, just drive the ball and try to force things to happen. I want him to attack first.”.

    Recent findings suggest that here lies the challenge I encountered while analyzing the game against Nottingham: how do you describe intentionally provoked chaos, where there are barely any fixed patterns? Only a few predefined sequences can be identified within the positional framework. The crucial question, therefore, is: what reference points structure Bournemouth’s possession play, and which principles of play create this chaos? Or, put simply: what “tools” does Iraola use in his style of play? To answer this, the positional framework of the game against Nottingham will first be examined.

    According to recent reports, starting from a nominal 4-2-3-1 formation, Nottingham defended out of possession in a 4-4-1-1 or 4-5-1 structure. Nottingham focused primarily on defending and largely conceded possession to Bournemouth, a characteristic approach for the team. Under coach Simoes Espirito Santo, Nottingham has averaged just 40% possession this season.

    Recent findings suggest that bournemouth, meanwhile, operated in possession with a positional 2-4-4 or 2-3-2-3 structure, featuring wide wingers and full-backs. From this setup, Bournemouth attempted to break through Nottingham’s deep block. On the (left) No. 10 position, Kluivert stood out with his exceptional dribbling ability and high agility. Central midfielder Christie alternated between the deeper right half-space as a right-sided No. 10 and the No. 6 position.

    Nottingham was often forced back into their own half from an initially higher defensive pressing. When Nottingham attempted to press higher, Bournemouth’s center-backs positioned themselves wide, and goalkeeper Kepa moved up to form part of the back line. This made it nearly impossible for Nottingham’s lone striker to put significant pressure on the ball carrier. As a result, Nottingham dropped deep, retreated, and refrained from pressing the ball-carrying center-backs.

    In a recent development, „I sometimes value much more a player carrying the ball and forcing things to happen. I think when you play too positional – one, two touches to find a free man – you sometimes lose the initiative from the players to just take their man on and attack the spaces.” – Iraola.

    This approach meant that Bournemouth’s center-backs were frequently required to dribble forward against stationary opponents, forcing defenders to commit. This often created 5v4 or 4v4 situations on the flanks, caused by the strong lateral movements of striker Ouattara and attacking midfielder Kluivert, combined with the forward dribbling of the center-backs. When no passingoptions were available, the team didn’t rebuild play, as is typical for positionally oriented teams. Instead, Bournemouth’s left center-back, Huijsen, was occasionally seen dribbling directly at the opponent’s last defensive line. It can be concluded that one of Iraola’s key principles of play is to attack vertically with the ball as early as possible.

    Center-back Huijsen dribbles toward the final defensive line himself due to a lack of better-positioned deeper passing options.

    The situations on the flanks during the center-back’s dribbling were played out in various ways. Sometimes the ball was passed to the wide player on the wing, who was tasked with taking on a 1v1 duel. This player was consistently supported by the full-back in a dual-width setup.

    Recent findings suggest that particularly noteworthy were the positional rotations of the 3-4 players on the flanks. Full-backs, attacking midfielder Kluivert, striker Ouattara, and the winger frequently rotated out of their positions, occupying different spaces. What stood out was the consistent presence of a dynamic deep run within these rotations, forcing the opponent to cover the run and thereby creating space between their players.

    The positional rotations with deep runs create passing options.

    In a recent development, for example, the left-back Kerkez, during the center-back’s dribble, occasionally made deep runs into the half-space. Similarly, attacking midfielder Kluivert was often involved, sometimes shifting laterally to receive the ball and then driving forward at pace to attack the defensive block.

    According to recent reports, nottingham responded to this from the 30th minute by attempting to apply more pressure on Bournemouth’s ball-carrying center-backs. The 4-4-1-1 shape was adjusted by removing the man-marking on defensive midfielder Adams. Instead, Nottingham transitioned into a 4-4-2 setup, aiming to position Adams in the cover shadow and step out earlier to press the center-backs. However, Bournemouth’s goalkeeper Kepa played so high in the back line that he was still able to connect with the now even wider-positioned center-backs, allowing them to continue dribbling forward.

    The goalkeeper stepping into the back line creates a 4v2 situation, allowing the center-backs to dribble forward with less pressure from opponents.

    “I would say they have the freedom to risk a little bit in the dribbles.“ – Iraola.

    It has been revealed that another key principle of Bournemouth’s possession game is diagonal, vertical dribbling. These serve as a chaos factor and are constantly utilized across all positions. As long as no teammate is better positioned toward the opponent’s goal, players are given the freedom to dribble. The skillful dribblers on the wings, the striker, and attacking midfielder Kluivert fit perfectly into this principle. The spaces opened up through the aforementioned rotations, particularly between the opposing players on the flanks, were mostly attacked through dribbling rather than passing.

    Industry observers note that the core idea behind this focus on dribbling is closely aligned with the concept of relationism. The goal is to make the team’s decisions less predictable for the opponent and to create a certain degree of chaos. Traditional positional play often limits players’ individual freedom, which reduces the element of surprise. However, Iraola’s execution of possession football differs significantly from relationism.

    Recent findings suggest that instead of using a tighter structure to encourage combinations between players, rotations and larger distances between players are used to create spaces intended to be attacked through dribbling. It is crucial that these dribbles are always executed as vertical actions, continually putting the opponent under defensive pressure and thereby opening up other options.

    Due to the larger spaces on the flanks, many dribbles are initiated on the wing, supported by the dual-width occupation of the winger and full-back. To enforce a successful follow-up action against deep-lying opponents, proper box occupation is a fundamental requirement. Iraola’s teams often flood the opponent’s penalty area with up to seven players, forcing the opposition right in front of their own goal. The goal is not necessarily to find the open player but to increase the likelihood of winning the ball after a cross in the penalty area. Second balls also play a significant role in this approach.

    Recent findings suggest that risky dribbles have the additional advantage of provoking more frequent transition moments. When the opponent tries to transition offensively, they lose their compact defensive shape. Bournemouth’s flexible rest defense allows the ball to be immediately recovered after a loss of possession. Bournemouth’s rest defense typically consists of 3-4 players, depending on the attacking structure. In addition to the two center-backs, defensive midfielder Adams and the inverted, far-side full-back provide cover. If both full-backs or Adams are involved in the attack, Christie drops deeper to provide support and shifts closer to the ball.

    According to recent reports, on one hand, it’s important to highlight the excellent sense of positioning from the two central midfielders, Adams and Christie, in anticipating potential turnovers. Their ability to read these moments and their spatial awareness lead to many successful counter-pressing actions. On the other hand, the immediate pressure applied to the ball-carrying opponent after a turnover is notable, leaving the opposition with little opportunity to create controlled possession phases.

    It has been revealed that as a result, Nottingham’s offensive presence in the first half was minimal. Successful offensive transitions by Simoes Espirito Santo’s team were extremely rare.

    In a recent development, the rest-defense structure in the 21st minute consists of the inverted Kerkez, the shifting defensive midfielder Adams, and the center-backs. At the same time, the ball-near teammates position themselves in response to the dribble in a way that allows them to immediately apply pressure if needed.

    According to recent reports, another key principle of Bournemouth’s play is that after regaining possession, the first action is immediately directed forward. In contrast to traditionally positional teams, control is not sought through possession in chaotic situations but rather through constant transitions. The goal is to prevent the opponent from regaining their structure and settling into their usual rhythm. This creates intense pressure for Bournemouth’s opponents. As a result, Bournemouth often didn’t even need to break down Nottingham’s defensive block because the opponent never had the chance to regain their typical structure.

    According to recent reports, after recovering the ball, Bournemouth consistently looked to play forward into pressure. When positioned deeper (closer to their own goal), players in the forward zones immediately made runs into space to create vertical passing options. Even if the Bournemouth player who regained the ball was immediately under pressure, the first action was directed forward.

    If necessary, a long ball was played toward the opponent’s defensive line, with a focus on winning second balls. This pressing game with an emphasis on second balls—often referred to as “kick and rush”—generated additional forced transition situations, preventing the opponent from finding their usual shape. The fact that four of Bournemouth’s five goals against the typically deep-lying Nottingham team came from deliberately provoked transition moments highlights the effectiveness of this approach.

    In a recent development, in the second half, Nottingham switched to an attacking press in an attempt to create more scoring opportunities and overturn the 1-0 deficit. However, Nottingham was unable to pin Bournemouth in their own half as planned. Instead, Bournemouth played targeted long balls to one of their four advanced attackers or to the half-high positioned full-backs. Through a combination of winning second balls, dribbles, and central midfielders following up for lay-offs, Bournemouth was able to quickly progress into space and control the game from their own half. This led to Bournemouth scoring their second and third goals in quick succession. The final result was a resounding 5-0 victory for Iraola’s side.

    So, what exactly causes the chaos in Bournemouth’s possession play? In summary, it is a combination of the principles discussed: playing vertically as early as possible; dribbling diagonally and vertically as long as no player is better positioned toward the opponent’s goal; and making the first action after regaining possession a forward one. The focus on vertical zones (reference point: opponent players) and second balls (reference point: the opponent’s goal) creates an intense and dynamic style of play that prevents the opponent from settling into their usual structure. Bournemouth is further aided by their attacking press, which was not analyzed in detail in this article but consistently provokes additional transition situations.

    What can other teams take away from Bournemouth’s possession approach without abandoning their own philosophy? One lesson is the courage to consistently seek depth, provided the team has appropriate counter-pressing structures in place. Additionally, the dynamism of individual actions at Bournemouth is remarkable. Rarely have I seen such explosive runs into depth from other teams.

    It has been revealed that the final question is: what do the teams mentioned by Guardiola in the aforementioned interview have in common? All of them attack the depth swiftly and frequently, making the game incredibly dynamic and intense. This forces the opponent to make decisions faster. After all, the main difference between good and very good players is the time it takes to make a good decision.

    It has been revealed that my recommendation is to watch games from 30 years ago. It quickly becomes apparent that football has become faster and more demanding.

    “For me, the players are better than in 2003. They have to do the same things, but much faster. The physical demands are ridiculous. I doubt I could have played at this rhythm.” – Iraola.

    #142014. NFL Monday Night Football preview: Joe Burrow, Jayden Daniels meet in significant game for Bengals and Commanders

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1002 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    NFL Monday Night Football preview: Joe Burrow, Jayden Daniels meet in significant game for Bengals and Commanders

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Joe Burrow and Jayden Daniels have plenty in common.
    • They starred at LSU and each won a Heisman Trophy.
    • It has been revealed that burrow comes into Monday night's game as the NFL MVP favorite with his Cincinnati Bengals at 7-2 and in first place of the AFC North.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Joe Burrow and Jayden Daniels have plenty in common.

    They starred at LSU and each won a Heisman Trophy. They both were high picks in the NFL Draft and have had success in the pros. But, like their LSU legacies, Burrow has done just a little more.

    It has been revealed that burrow comes into Monday night's game as the NFL MVP favorite with his Cincinnati Bengals at 7-2 and in first place of the AFC North. He is on pace for more than 5,000 yards and 50 passing touchdowns.

    "I mean, it would be impossible to say that anyone is playing better," Bengals coach Zac Taylor remarked after Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers last week. "I'm not watching every game ... but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth.".

    The Washington Commanders are trying to stay in the NFC East race at 3-5-1, but their entire season has been a challenge. Daniels has been good but not quite to the level he reached when he was NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2024.

    Sources indicate that the game is about more than just the respective quarterbacks. The Bengals have improved around Burrow, protecting him better and with a defense that has improved since an offseason trade with the Giants for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II.

    The Commanders' situation around Daniels hasn't been as great. The offense is thin on playmakers after Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, though running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return from an injury on Monday night. There have been plenty of questions about head coach Dan Quinn's job security. The Commanders stayed alive in the NFC East race with a win over the Upcoming York Giants last week, but they don't have much margin for error anymore.

    It is an interesting contrast between the teams, and with two star quarterbacks from LSU taking center stage, Baton Rouge will be tuning in.

    Sources indicate that cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, left, and Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels talk following a preseason NFL football game Monday, Aug. 18, 2025, in Landover, Md. (AP Photo/Nick Wass).

    Some results on Sunday dictate this answer. The Steelers lost to the Eagles, a bad loss that dropped them to 6-4 and two losses behind the Bengals in the AFC North race. Elsewhere, the Giants pulled off an upset win over the Jaguars to improve to 6-3-1, increasing their lead in the NFC East. The Commanders already dug themselves a hole early in the season and the Giants continue to win games. The Bengals are pushing for the No. 1 seed in the AFC and nobody in that race can afford bad losses, but Washington probably needs the win more. The Commanders need all the wins they can get to stay in the playoff picture.

    Sources indicate that the Bengals are coming along well on defense but still have issues covering tight ends. The 685 yards allowed to tight ends this season is tied for second-worst in the NFL, according to Pro Football Reference. The team they're tied with? The Commanders, so Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki could be a factor on Monday night, too. For Washington's offense to thrive, it needs some pass catchers to step up around Jayden Daniels. Okonkwo is having a solid season with 27 catches for 263 yards, but the Commanders probably need more from him on Monday night against a defense that is vulnerable against tight ends. Okonkwo has 15 targets the past two games, so Washington is trying to get him more involved. It's a good matchup for Okonkwo to have his biggest game of the season.

    Just how good is Cincinnati's offense? That's basically what this handicap boils down to. Respected money pushed this line up from Bengals -4 to -6 (in Washington), but that's been the point of resistance. Joe Burrow & Co. have scored at least 31 points in five victories (4-1 against the spread), while the Commanders haven't lost by more than seven points in any of their past five games. Ultimately, both defenses are similar in yards per play allowed (Washington at 5.4 YPP; Cincinnati at 5.5 YPP), but I think the Bengals' offense (third in NFL at 6.2 YPP) is too potent for the Commanders to keep this within the number over the course of four quarters. — Ben Fawkes.

    Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub.

    Fantasy hopes are high as the Bengals and Commanders hold a 54.5-point total for Monday. Here are three themes to track from a fantasy perspective.

    1. What is Jacory Croskey-Merritt ready to do? Washington's running game has been stuck in neutral all year (25th in DVOA), in part because of JCM's groin injury. He's missed the past four games, but he's also averaging a mere 3.6 YPC when active. Nonetheless, he's the best natural runner the team has.

    Sources indicate that 2. Can anything stop the Cincinnati passing game? MVP favorite Joe Burrow has been too good to be true over his past five starts, piling up 20 touchdown passes and 1,624 passing yards (he's also rushed for a couple of scores). Ja'Marr Chase (WR4) and Tee Higgins (WR7) are both smashing this year, and TE Mike Gesicki has somehow scored six times on just 20 receptions.

    3. Who emerges among the Washington pass catchers? Stefon Diggs is still getting by on guile and experience, but he's making only 6.5 yards per target. Antonio Williams has played better of late, and tight end Chig Okonkwo is a target earner, though he hasn't scored a touchdown yet. Jayden Daniels hasn't run much for a month, so he'll need to keep the offense moving with his arm. — Scott Pianowski.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that happy Thanksgiving week!
    • Every league is different, so I'm focusing on players who are under 50% rostered on Yahoo.
    • Tuesday features three games, while Saturday has five.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that happy Thanksgiving week! There are no games Thursday, and it's a tough week to stream, with only two days — Tuesday (three games) and Saturday (five) — with fewer than nine games on the slate. There's some good news on the injury front: Brandon Ingram is back and set to make his Clippers debut Monday against Houston, and we should see Austin Reaves (heel) return for the Lakers as well. On the other side, we lost Evan Mobley to a toe injury and Dylan Harper to a hip injury.

    Every league is different, so I'm focusing on players who are under 50% rostered on Yahoo.

    Tuesday features three games, while Saturday has five. The Magic and Wizards are the only teams playing on both slates, so streaming from them is my priority given the circumstances in Week 6.

    Da Silva is my top Tuesday-and-Saturday pickup. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) still out, he's playing 29.9 minutes per game and averaging 13.8 points and 3.2 3s on the season, and he scored 18 points with 4 3s at Washington on Sunday. Orlando has a tough matchup against Detroit, then gets an easier game against Washington on Saturday, the front end of a back-to-back. Add him for points, 3s and low turnovers. He's scored at least 12 points in five of his last six contests.

    Industry observers note that washington only plays twice, but both games are on the light nights: Tuesday against Boston and Saturday against Orlando. He's a stocks play, averaging 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks in 24.9 minutes this season, with 5.5 rebounds and 1.3 blocks over his last six games. He had 12 points with 3 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 block, 4 3s and 3 turnovers Sunday against Orlando, so there's at least some recent success to point towards.

    The backup center for the Magic looks to have passed Nikola Vučević on the depth chart. He's averaging 6.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 0.7 steals and 0.8 blocks on 86% shooting from the field in 18.0 minutes over his last six games. He won't wow you by any means, but extra boards and a strong FG% can help in 9-cat. Feel free to ignore if you're in a points league.

    Kelly Oubre Jr., SF/PF, Indiana Pacers (36% rostered): A top-55 player over the last two weeks in 9-cat, Oubre is producing 15.7 points, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks, with at least 14 points in six straight games. He's worth holding as long as he keeps starting. Indy has a weird schedule, playing on Monday and then a back-to-back on Friday and Saturday.

    Latest Update: Draymond Green jabs at critics saying he needs to score more: 'That would never be my mindset'

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Draymond Green rarely, if ever, refuses an opportunity to jab back at his critics.
    • Following the Golden State Warriors' 88-87 win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday, the veteran forward had plenty to say to those who believe he's not carrying enough of the scoring burden with Stephen Curry sidelined due to an abdominal tear.
    • Green scored 9 points in the Warriors' win, his highest total of the season thus far.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Draymond Green rarely, if ever, refuses an opportunity to jab back at his critics.

    Following the Golden State Warriors' 88-87 win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday, the veteran forward had plenty to say to those who believe he's not carrying enough of the scoring burden with Stephen Curry sidelined due to an abdominal tear.

    Green scored 9 points in the Warriors' win, his highest total of the season thus far. But scoring more has never been his role and he doesn't intend to change that, even with the team's top scorer out.

    Recent findings suggest that "I'm never going to, in Year 15, be like 'Oh, man, Steph's out — it's my chance,'" Green told reporters, via The Athletic's Jason Jones. "When I was in Year 6, it was my chance, and I would do what I do.

    "But Year 15? That would never be my mindset," he added. "As someone who can do a multitude of things on the basketball court, I would never deduce myself down to you gotta go score.".

    In a recent development, all nine of Green's points on Sunday came in the first quarter when he hit three 3-pointers. Green mentioned after the game that Warriors coach Steve Kerr told him to look to shoot from the corner. That helped Golden State run out to a 27-22 lead after the opening 12 minutes of play.

    It has been revealed that the Celtics went ahead with a third-quarter surge, leading by 11 at one point. But the Warriors tightened up on defense, allowing them to chip away at the second-half deficit. Golden State finally took an 88-86 lead with 2:38 remaining in regulation on a 3-pointer from Brandin Podziemski.

    According to recent reports, on Boston's final possession, Green prevented Jayson Tatum from driving to the basket and forced him to take a fadeaway jumper. But the 16-footer missed and the Warriors got their ninth win of the season.

    Recent findings suggest that tatum was held to 4 points in the second half with Green defending him. That's exactly what Golden State needs Green to do, according to Kerr. Green offered to come off the bench if it would help the team, but Kerr remarked his defense is too valuable throughout the game.

    "I told him I had no desire to bring him on the bench because we've got to dig this thing out with defense," Kerr remarked, via The Athletic. "And he remains one of the great defenders in the league. He demonstrated that tonight.".

    Green is averaging 3.6 points in 14 games this season. If that continues, it would be his lowest scoring average since his rookie campaign in 2012-13. He's also grabbing 4.8 rebounds and dishing out 6.3 assists while shooting 33% on 21 3-point attempts.

    Inter Milan U19: Team Analysis – MH

    📅 05 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 05.03.2025 in den Kategorien Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • Industry observers note that inter Milan’s U19 team is the only side in this season’s UEFA Youth League to have won all their matches so far, finishing the group stage of the “Youth Champions League” in first place.
    • Recent findings suggest that inter Milan generally builds up in a nominal 4-3-3 shape.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 05.03.2025 in den Kategorien Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.

    Industry observers note that inter Milan’s U19 team is the only side in this season’s UEFA Youth League to have won all their matches so far, finishing the group stage of the “Youth Champions League” in first place. They also secured victory in the knockout playoff round and will now face Bayern Munich U19 in the Round of 16. This analysis will take a closer look at Inter Milan’s tactical structures and mechanisms under head coach Andrea Zanchetta in the Youth League while also considering possible approaches against them.

    Recent findings suggest that inter Milan generally builds up in a nominal 4-3-3 shape. A key role is played by the midfield trio, consisting of the two number eights, Topalovic and Venturini, alongside the single pivot, Mattia Zanchetta. Zanchetta frequently drops between the center-backs, taking on a key role in deep buildup, while the two eights serve as connectors and overload players in the transition from deeper buildup into more advanced areas. According to the Italian Wikipedia, head coach Andrea Zanchetta is the father of Mattia Zanchetta.

    Inter’s defensive structure varies depending on the opponent and pressing height. In mid-block and high-pressing phases, they defend in a narrow 4-3-2-1, a compact 4-3-3, or a 4-4-2, depending on the opposition’s structure. When defending deeper, they shift into a 4-1-4-1, with Zanchetta holding his position as the single pivot shielding the backline.

    Industry observers note that as the central striker, either Lavelli or Spinaccè leads the line. Since both share a similar physical, robust playing style, this analysis will primarily refer to Spinaccè, who has started in recent matches. On the right wing, Pieri is a fixed starter, known for his strong 1v1 abilities. On the opposite flank, head coach Zanchetta has rotated more frequently, but he has consistently relied on technically strong, dribble-oriented wingers.

    Industry observers note that to build up against high pressing, Inter relies on certain patterns that make it more difficult for the opponent to press successfully. A frequent observation is that the center-backs move wide while the full-backs push up along the touchline. At the same time, the single pivot Zanchetta and/or the number eight Topalovic drop deep to lure the opposition’s midfield out of the center. The longer the possession phase lasts near their own penalty area, the more likely it is that both the pivot and the number eight drop into the center-back positions. The now-vacated central space is occupied by the other number eight, Venturini, and the frequently dropping center-forward Spinaccè. When buildup occurs on the right side, Topalovic often stays on the far side to stretch the central area further. The wingers act as additional passing options by tucking into the half-spaces. From this structure, the opponent can be bypassed using vertical-layoff combinations in the half-space.

    Recent findings suggest that the primary goal of the buildup is often a pass to the target man Spinaccè, who either uses Venturini as a layoff option or directly switches play to the wing. By pulling apart the central space through the movements of Topalovic and Zanchetta, the goalkeeper typically initiates buildup through the wide center-backs, who frequently play a direct pass to the dropping striker via the now-open diagonal deep passing lane. Particularly noteworthy are the anticipatory movements of the layoff options in these combinations. The attacking number eight, Venturini, excels at positioning himself to receive layoffs from the back-to-goal striker Spinaccè, ensuring continuity in progression.

    Recent findings suggest that if only Zanchetta drops between the center-backs to form the resulting back three, the left-sided number eight, Topalovic, and the right-sided number eight, Venturini, move into the half-spaces to receive when the center-backs are in possession. Through a vertical-layoff combination involving one of the eights, the now-advancing pivot Zanchetta, and the dropping center-forward Spinaccè, the midfield can be swiftly bypassed, allowing the ball to be switched to the wing in the opponent’s half.

    To effectively press Inter’s buildup directly, a hybrid pressing approach combining man- and space-orientation could be a viable strategy. A particularly crucial role could be assigned to the ball-far holding midfielder, who could operate positionally to close passing lanes, preventing deep balls into the target man Spinaccè while also ensuring that the central space cannot be stretched. Additionally, an aggressive step-out from a center-back would be necessary to avoid numerical inferiority in midfield. On the ball-near side, increased pressure could be applied through man-oriented marking to maximize pressing intensity.

    Through hybrid pressing, the center can be occupied, and the typical passing lane can be blocked. The downside is the numerical disadvantage on the ball-far side and the man-to-man marking on the last line.

    It has been revealed that even against teams that press deeper, certain patterns can be observed in Inter Milan U19’s buildup. From their usual 4-3-3 structure with a single pivot and two number eights, they transition into a three-man buildup shape against opponents using a two-striker system. To achieve this, Zanchetta drops between the center-backs, who move wider, while the full-backs push higher along the touchline. However, Zanchetta plays a flexible role, shifting between a central center-back position and his original pivot role, making himself available in midfield depending on the situation.

    Sources indicate that this three-man buildup creates upcoming passing connections designed to pose problems for the opponent. A key role is played by Topalovic and Venturini, who drop closer to the buildup to fill the emerging gap between the midfield and the first buildup line. The buildup is primarily conducted through the half-spaces and the wide areas. The ball-near number eight moves into the half-space to overload it, while Venturini, from the right half-space, moves into an advanced position, and Topalovic, from the left half-space, stays closer to the buildup zone, occasionally even dropping into the first line. The ball-far number eight occupies the center.

    In a recent development, due to this asymmetry between the two eights, the wingers on each side have slightly different roles. On the right side, where Venturini often occupies the advanced half-space, the right winger stays wider, creating double width with the full-back. On the left side, since Topalovic supports deeper in the buildup, the left winger frequently moves into the half-space, opening the lane for the overlapping full-back on the outside.

    Recent findings suggest that additionally, Spinaccè overloads the half-space by shifting ball-near and dropping deeper. Particularly on the left side, a diagonal deep pass from the wide-positioned center-back in the back three can find either the winger or the striker in a diagonal alignment. This escadinha staggering provides multiple layoff options. The ultimate goal after playing through the half-space is to create a 1v1 situation on the wing, allowing the dribbling-strong wingers or advancing full-backs to be isolated and attack down the flank.

    Through the typical half-space overload, the wide area can be opened for a 1v1 situation involving the advancing full-back.

    Industry observers note that the follow-up action is usually a cross into the penalty area. This is typically occupied by the aerially strong striker, the ball-far winger, and Topalovic. In the second line, Zanchetta and Venturini can win second balls.

    According to recent reports, one of the key aspects of Inter Milan’s game is their man-marking high press. With the exception of the match against Manchester City, coach Zanchetta’s team has consistently relied on man-marking and aggressive pressing in advanced areas. This approach frequently creates dangerous transition moments by forcing early turnovers.

    Recent findings suggest that while striker Spinaccè and the right winger are primarily responsible for initiating the press, Topalovic and Zanchetta operate in central areas. Zanchetta, known for his strength in duels, pushes far forward from his usual deeper pivot position to press opposing midfielders and win the ball in central areas. The offensively oriented number eight, Venturini, is deliberately kept out of direct 1v1 defensive duels in the center and instead takes responsibility for a potentially advancing full-back. On the opposite side, the opposing full-back is covered by Inter’s winger.

    It has been revealed that the pressing is almost always triggered by Spinaccè from a slightly left-sided position. He presses the goalkeeper while blocking the passing lane to the left center-back. This forces the opponent’s buildup toward the wing, where Inter engages in their man-oriented pressing. In particular, the ball-far midfielder, Topalovic, often abandons his direct man-marking after the opponent is forced to play toward the far-side wing. Instead, he drops back toward the defensive line to create numerical superiority and ensure that the center-backs can step out aggressively without leaving gaps in the last line.

    Recent findings suggest that A possible solution against this man-marking press could involve putting the opposing center-backs in a dilemma. By having the strikers drop deep, they could force the center-backs to abandon their cover in the last line. Since Inter Milan’s full-backs are less dominant in defensive 1v1 situations, wingers making deep diagonal runs into the vacated spaces could create a favorable scenario. Once the press is triggered, these wingers should be played into 1v1 situations through deep passes. This either forces the physically strong center-backs out of the last line or creates a numerical superiority in midfield that can be exploited.

    In a recent development, another possible approach could involve a high-positioned, inverted left-back. By dropping into the space between the opponent’s forward and midfield lines, he could create a central 1v1 against Venturini, who is not as defensively strong.

    Depending on the opponent, Inter may drop slightly deeper and defend in a 4-3-3 or 4-4-2 mid-block shape. This adjustment depends on the opposition’s buildup structure. The fundamental goal is to maintain numerical parity against the opponent’s buildup line, allowing Inter to transition into aggressive man-marking and press forward. Against a three-man buildup, they press in a 4-3-3 shape, while against a four-man buildup, they shift into a 4-4-2. A key emphasis is placed on central compactness, making it more difficult for the opponent to progress through the middle.

    Once the ball is shifted to one side, Inter looks to apply pressure and enforce man-marking, similar to their approach in the high press. Zanchetta frequently pushes forward aggressively on the ball-near side to put pressure on the opponent’s central midfielders and create ball-winning opportunities.

    While the full-backs also push high to apply pressure, the center-backs primarily serve as defensive cover. However, when the opposition’s strikers drop deeper, the center-backs do not follow them to avoid leaving gaps in the defensive line. Instead, Inter presses with one less player in the first line to compensate for the opponent’s numerical superiority in midfield. Even in these situations, the opponent is guided toward one side, where Inter then looks to regain possession. To execute this, the first pressing line must initially cut off the passing lane to one of the defenders, allowing the opponent to maintain more possession and reducing Inter’s ability to transition into their man-marking press.

    Especially in the low block, Inter Milan manages to make the field so compact that progression becomes extremely difficult. From a 4-1-4-1 structure, they compress the space just in front of their own penalty area. Zanchetta operates between the lines as a space-oriented pivot in front of the defense. When the opponent shifts play to one side, Zanchetta also moves laterally and looks to engage an opposing player.

    As the central players shift heavily toward the ball side, defensive numerical superiority is often created near the ball, allowing Inter to apply pressure. The ball-far number eight secures the central area, while the ball-far winger stays wide when the opponent maintains width on both flanks to prevent switches of play. This enables the last defensive line to shift further toward the ball side, allowing the ball-near center-back to step out aggressively while still being covered.

    Inter Milan’s U19 team manages to challenge opponents through a well-organized and versatile defensive structure. They can adapt to various pressing heights, with their difficult-to-play man-marking high press frequently creating dangerous transition moments close to the opponent’s goal.

    Recent findings suggest that in possession, Inter also succeeds in reaching the opponent’s penalty area frequently through a very direct approach aimed at attacking depth. The key to this is a well-coordinated midfield and a striker who can act as a target player, holding up the ball with his back to goal. Most of Inter’s combinations are designed to create a 1v1 situation on the wing, where both the advancing full-backs and the wingers are very difficult to defend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Dallas Cowboys and Tennessee Titans played one of the wildest games of Week 11, and it ended with the two teams combining to make some NFL history.
    • The scorigami only happened because the Titans scored a garbage-time touchdown with less than one minute in the game.
    • TEN 30 - DAL 51 | 0:31 left in 4th👀 Scorigami Watch100% chance, most likely Scorigami: 51-30.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Dallas Cowboys and Tennessee Titans played one of the wildest games of Week 11, and it ended with the two teams combining to make some NFL history. The Cowboys beat the Titans 51-30, which is notable because it marked the first time that exact final score occurred in the NFL's 107-year history.

    The scorigami only happened because the Titans scored a garbage-time touchdown with less than one minute in the game. With Tennessee trailing 51-23, Cam Ward hit Calvin Ridley for a 12-yard touchdown pass, and at that point, the Titans decided to kick the extra point. If the kick had missed, there wouldn't have been a scorigami, because 51-29 has happened before, but Joey Slye's kick went through and that ultimately gave us the 1,101st final score in NFL history.

    TEN 30 - DAL 51 | 0:31 left in 4th👀 Scorigami Watch100% chance, most likely Scorigami: 51-30.

    Industry observers note that if the Titans hadn't gotten into the end zone on their final drive, the game wouldn't have ended in a scorigami, because 51-23 has happened before. If the Titans had successfully gone for two, we also wouldn't have gotten a scorigami, because 51-31 has happened before.

    For a game to end in a scorigami, you need a few bizarre things to happen and that was certainly the case here. The main thing that happened is that the Cowboys offense went off. Dak Prescott totaled five touchdowns on a day when the Cowboys scored seven. If you throw in a Brandon Aubrey field goal, that's how the Cowboys got to 51, and any time you see a team put up at least 50 points, there's always a solid chance of a scorigami.

    The Cowboys missed a two-point conversion in this game, but that didn't matter, because even if they had hit it, 53-30 would have also been a scorigami.

    On the Titans' end, the garbage-time touchdown played a substantial part in the scorigami, but the only reason Tennessee got to 30 points is that they scored one of the craziest touchdowns of the season.

    Nobody touched Carnell Tate and he scores!TENvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cQ7sadUDLH.

    That's Carnell Tate going 59 yards for a score after not being touched by the Cowboys' defense.

    This marks the second straight week that the Cowboys have been involved in a scorigami. They also had a unique final score in their 46-40 loss to the 49ers. This marks the first time since 2016 that a team has been involved in scorigami in back-to-back games (the 49ers did it in Weeks 2 and 3 that season).

    Recent findings suggest that not to be outdone, this is also Tennessee's second scorigami of the season. The Titans were also involved in one back in a 43-36 loss to the Bengals in Week 8. This means the Titans' last two road games have both ended in a scorigami.

    Overall, there have been six scorigamis this year, already more than we saw in the entire 2025 season (five). This is turning into the year of the scorigami.

We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    DK Metcalf's forgettable 2026 season hit a upcoming low during Sunday's game between the Steelers and Eagles.

    Recent findings suggest that metcalf was ejected from the game after he appeared to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye in the third quarter. It was Metcalf's second unsportsmanlike penalty of the game, which led to his ejection. His first unnecessary roughness penalty occurred early in the third quarter after he got into a shoving match with the Eagles' defense.

    Sunday's ejection marks Metcalf's third of his eight-season career since 2019, which puts him in jeopardy of being suspended as a repeat offender. His first ejection came in Week 10 of the 2021 season in a 17-0 loss at the Green Bay Packers when Metcalf grabbed Packers safety Henry Black's facemask during an altercation. That led to him being ejected for fighting, and he was fined $6,949 at the time.

    #Seahawks WR DK Metcalf has been ejected after this altercation with #Packers DB Henry Black.pic.twitter.com/Ry1jdhIOpd.

    Sources indicate that in Week 14 of the 2023 season, Metcalf fought San Francisco 49ers All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner. He body slammed Warner into the turf before grabbing the linebacker's facemask when fighting. He was ejected in the Seahawks' 28-16 defeat that day and fined $19,123 for fighting. The eight-year veteran was fined $11,941 by the NFL for taunting following Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Browns. He was suspended for the final two regular-season games of the 2025 season after getting into a physical altercation with a Lions fan, an incident in which Metcalf was sued but ultimately not charged. Metcalf returned for Pittsburgh's AFC wild card game against the Texans, but he had a costly drop early in the game that set the tone for Pittsburgh's 30-6 loss. The NFL league office will certainly be reviewing his latest interaction with DeJean to determine his latest fine amount and/or whether or not a suspension is warranted.

    "They say it's going to a good cause, so I might as well win Walter Payton Man of the Year," Metcalf remarked this summer when asked if he is tired of giving money to the NFL via fines. "So no, I'm not tired of it.".

    It has been revealed that metcalf appeared to be frustrated with the Eagles' physicality downfield on Sunday. Philadelphia's secondary blanketed him on an incomplete pass moments before his altercation with DeJean.

    DK Metcalf has been ejected in PhillyCBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J.

    Metcalf caught just one of four targets for two yards. His only reception occurred on Pittsburgh's first offensive series.

    Industry observers note that A Pro Bowler with Seattle, Metcalf is just two years into a four-year, $132 million contract he signed with the Steelers shortly after Pittsburgh traded for him. Metcalf had just 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns in 2025, a career low in receptions and yardage, plus the second-fewest touchdowns in a season of his career. 2026 has not been much of an improvement, with just 35 catches for 432 yards and two touchdowns this season entering Sunday's game. Metcalf's 12.3 yards per reception, 6.2 yards per target and 40.0% success rate on the year would all be career lows if the season ended today.

    The Steelers could possibly try to move Metcalf this offseason, but his massive contract will undoubtedly make any trade difficult.

    In the meantime, the Steelers will continue to try to win games with a subpar receiving corps.

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1169 w)

    Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1169 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He demonstrated few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    The Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the significant-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    Industry observers note that coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    In a recent development, the Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by fresh owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    The Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    Industry observers note that eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.

    Industry observers note that may, 29, split this past season between the St. Louis Cardinals and World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers.     Recent findings suggest that rotation help was a priority for a White Sox team that reached the postseason for the first time since 2021, but used openers and bullpen games regularly throughout the season.     Castillo struggled badly (30 runs in 31 innings) after coming over from the Seattle Mariners at the trade deadline, and finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder issue. Even after the injuries, May still lives in the mid-to-upper-90s with his sinker, and pitch data models are fond of his sweeper and curveball. It is not the best sign, though, that the Brewers, who know pitching as well as any team, couldn't fully unlock May after making him their big deadline rotation addition. Still, the combination of age and high-octane stuff makes him a nice upside play ...

    According to recent reports, may made two starts and three relief appearances during Milwaukee's postseason run. If the White Sox opt to use bullpen games again next year, he is familiar and capable in that role. The signing pushes Chicago's projected 2027 payroll up to $120 million, per FanGraphs, well above the team's $102 million figure this past season.

    The White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 and became the first team in baseball history to reach the postseason after back-to-back 100-loss seasons. They lost 100 games in each of the three previous seasons, going 61-101 in 2023, 41-121 in 2024, and 60-102 in 2025.

    According to recent reports, the annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some desperately needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    Sources indicate that otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the notable offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Tuesday's hot stove happenings.

    Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic. There is some reluctance to trade for players with only one year of control because games could be lost to a work stoppage next year, but pitching is so in-demand that at least some clubs are exploring a deal for Gore.

    Industry observers note that now 27, Gore is one of only six pitchers to make at least 30 starts in each of the last three years. His under-the-hood numbers (3.87 FIP and 4.19 expected ERA) were much better than his 4.58 actual ERA, plus he has long been considered to have untapped upside. Gore will give you innings, at minimum, and there's a chance his best days are ahead of him.

    Recent findings suggest that the Red Sox are exploring the trade market for righties Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo, according to WEEI. They are also believed to be preparing to trade Jarren Duran, reports MassLive.com. Duran is a potential non-tender candidate if the Red Sox are unable to find a trade partner prior to Friday's deadline. The Mariners and Phillies are among the teams that are "poking around.".

    Crawford, Houck, and Ovideo all missed significant time with injuries in 2026 (Crawford has not appeared in an MLB game since 2024) and are far down Boston's rotation depth chart. Duran has been pushed out of the everyday lineup by the recent Jake Bauers signing. Exploring trades for these four players in a seller's market is a sensible approach.

    The Mets had an in-person meeting with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Monday, reports the Upcoming York Post. Owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those in attendance, according to SNY. Skubal and agent Scott Boras will meet with the Blue Jays, Dodgers, Padres, and potentially two other teams in the coming days.

    In a recent development, skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Boras clients. Nolan McLean and Christian Scott give the Mets two promising young arms to build around, but they need to improve the rotation around them, and Skubal would give the club a no-doubt ace to lead the pitching staff.

    The pitching-needy Cubs have shown interest in free agent lefty Trevor Rogers, reports The Athletic. Chicago needs multiple starters this offseason and has cast a wide net in their search. Justin Steele (UCL) and Ben Brown (neck), ostensibly the Cubs' No. 1 and 2 starters, are both recovering from surgeries, and Brown is expected to miss the start of 2027.

    Sources indicate that we ranked Rogers as the third-best free agent available this offseason because he is very good as is, and because he'll make analytical models hum with the quality of his arsenal and strike-throwing. Nine pitchers made at least nine starts for the Cubs in 2026 and only two -- Javier Assad and Edward Cabrera -- at the moment remain under contract/team control.

    The AL East rival Orioles and Yankees are among the teams with interest in free agent slugger Randy Arozarena, according to the Baltimore Banner and Fresh York Post. The O's also have some interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr. Other than Dylan Beavers and maybe Tyler O'Neill, Baltimore's outfield is wide open right now. They have DH at-bats available too.

    In a recent development, it is likely the Yankees checked in on Arozarena out of due diligence more than serious interest. His righty bat would help their lefty-heavy lineup, though he would be a clunky roster fit as a corner outfielder who really needs to DH on a team that already has plenty of corner outfielders who really need to DH. If Arozarena's market is slow to develop, perhaps Upcoming York would pounce.

    Teams around the league believe the Rockies are more open to trading All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman now than they were at the trade deadline, reports MLB Network. Colorado is stated to have set a very high asking price for Goodman, who in 2026 became just the tenth primary catcher with a 40-homer season. He hit more homers on the road (25) than at Coors Field (16) too.

    Ryan Jeffers and Carson Kelly represent viable free agent alternatives to Goodman as right-handed offense-first catchers, though Goodman is several years younger than both and will have a lower salary the next three years through arbitration. Teams will likely feel more confident in Goodman holding his production for another few years than Jeffers and Kelly.
