    #141987. Industry News: The Timing Game – MH

    📅 31 Mar 2025 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4137 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Spielverlagerung ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: The Timing Game – MH

    📅 31 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4137 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 31.03.2025 in den Kategorien Tactical Theory mit 1 Kommentar.
    • The Timing Game describes a playing philosophy in which the right moment of an action is crucial.
    • “Brighton is a master of passing the ball to the free man but recognising when to pass the ball to the free man and moving at the right time.” – Pep Guardiola.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 31.03.2025 in den Kategorien Tactical Theory mit 1 Kommentar.

    The Timing Game describes a playing philosophy in which the right moment of an action is crucial. It not only allows pressing traps to be reversed but also enables teams to break down deep defensive blocks with precision. In the Premier League, Brighton’s then-manager Roberto De Zerbi took this tactical approach to a latest level.

    “Brighton is a master of passing the ball to the free man but recognising when to pass the ball to the free man and moving at the right time.” – Pep Guardiola.

    It has been revealed that the core idea of the Timing Game is to react to the opponent’s movement at precisely the right moment. Pressing traps can be reversed by first triggering and manipulating the opponent’s press and then bypassing it through changes in speed and direction. Since opposition pressing actions are highly dynamic, this approach is particularly effective against high-pressing teams. Consequently, the Timing Game allows teams to dominate pressing situations in their own buildup play. Additionally, because opponent movements can be triggered independently of the game phase, the Timing Game can also be applied against deep defensive blocks.

    Regarding the role of timing in De Zerbi’s buildup play, René Maric (RM) explained in a 2023 interview with SkySports:.

    Industry observers note that „The biggest thing in the build-up is the control of rhythm. If you look at Guardiola, he does it with the speed of the passes and then they carry the ball when they don’t have pressure. De Zerbi does it more with the moment of the pass, the lure, the sole on the ball, opening space with the pass rather than the carry. How you control the rhythm and progress through space will be big in the future. That development has already started.“.

    It has been revealed that this article examines the dimensions and functioning of the Timing Game. Additionally, it analyzes the impact of a team’s own positioning, as well as the manipulation, anticipation, and triggering of the opponent’s press (or movements). The following sections will then explore the action of bypassing the opponent, the potential issues that arise within the Timing Game, and possible solutions to these challenges.

    This section is an attempt to highlight the various facets of the Timing Game and football in general. Different playing philosophies prioritize different dimensions. In the Timing Game described here, particular focus is placed on the timing of dynamics in relation to the opponent.

    To gain a better understanding of the principles of the Timing Game, the following section presents and explains its different dimensions. This makes it clear how the Timing Game differs from the focus of positional play and relationism but can also be combined with them. Although the game dimensions are less important for the practical implementation of the Timing Game, they can be useful for further developing this concept or other coaching philosophies.

    The most key dimension of the Timing Game is the temporal dimension. The crucial factors are the speed and timing of decision-making. The timing of a progressive action should generally coincide with the opponent’s movement. The primary focus is therefore on the exact moment of an action.

    A second key dimension is that of dynamics. The dynamic dimension of the Timing Game revolves around explosiveness and changes in rhythm. Changes in dynamics can be decisive both in relation to one’s own play and in terms of directional shifts in relation to the opponent. Ultimately, the goal is to create the strongest possible reciprocal acceleration in the opponent.

    In the dimension of individual performance factors, the focus is on footballing competencies such as technical and athletic abilities. In the Timing Game, ball control is a crucial factor, as it significantly affects a player’s pressing resistance. Ball control involves both the ability to recognize a situation and the technical capability to handle the ball under pressure at any time. This skill is particularly crucial in the Timing Game, as it provides an advantage during the opponent’s pressing phase.

    Sources indicate that the causal-relational dimension deals with the cause-and-effect principle in interactions between teammates and opponents. There is a causal relationship both between the opponent’s defensive approach and the method of bypassing them, as well as between a teammate’s action and the resulting ball action. The following examples illustrate this:.

    Recent findings suggest that in relationism, interactions between teammates are particularly emphasized to enable optimal interplay. Due to the complexity of this dimension, I have linked MR’s seminar “The Future of the Game” here.

    Industry observers note that in the spatial dimension, the focus is on controlling specific zones of the pitch. This is particularly crucial in positional play, where the aim is to control the game through ball possession and spatial occupation. In the Timing Game, however, the goal is to reach the space behind the opponent. Since this space is constantly changing, it cannot strictly be defined as a fixed pitch zone. However, the spatial dimension does play a role in the preparatory positioning of the Timing Game. This article contains a dedicated section on the optimal positioning in preparation for the Timing Game.

    In the Timing Game, the moment of an action is primarily decisive. The moment of action is always triggered by the opponent’s movement. The more intense the opponent’s movement, the easier it is to bypass them. This is because, once the Timing Game is triggered, the opponent should be bypassed as diagonally opposed to their movement as possible. This forces the opponent into a maximal change of direction and dynamics.

    The pressing near one’s own penalty area is bypassed diagonally opposite to the direction of the press.

    A temporal advantage is created over the opponent, who initially has to accelerate in the opposite direction and loses time. The space that opens up behind the advancing opponent can be played most effectively. Representing the functioning of the Timing Game, the principle of “Lure and Shock” could be used. The opponent is first “lured” into the movement and then “shocked” by being bypassed.

    It has been revealed that the Timing Game is particularly effective during the opponent’s transition from a deeper to a higher pressing setup. At the moment of transition between ordered pressing phases, the opponent’s structure is often lacking, as the distances between the players change. Additionally, movement is present on all positions of the opponent, which can be exploited for the Timing Game. The direction of the opponent’s movement is also crucial, as during the transition from a deeper to a higher pressing phase, vertical movement away from the goal dominates, allowing spaces towards the opponent’s goal to be exploited.

    According to recent reports, this specific moment of the opponent’s pressing transition into a higher setup cannot be found in the classic phase model of the game according to Van Gaal. Depending on the perspective, it would be classified as part of either the team’s own possession phase or the opponent’s possession phase, even though it is significantly more complex and interesting than other possession situations. The opponent is essentially in a type of defensive transition into attack from the opponent’s ball possession, while the own team takes advantage of this moment and transitions from their own ball possession into a kind of offensive transition.

    Industry observers note that the Timing Game, however, does not only work during transitions between different pressing setups, but also independently of the game phase, and thus also within the framework of the opponent’s attacking press. The opponent’s movement in attacking pressing usually does not need to be triggered additionally. Instead, it is more about anticipating the moment when the opponent’s attacking press is triggered. At the moment of pressing initiation, there is a very high dynamic on multiple positions of the opponent in (diagonal) vertical directions, which allows the pressing to be bypassed with suitable movements at the moment of initiation. Particularly, the opponent’s pressing traps can be bypassed at the moment of initiation through a corresponding pre-rehearsed anticipation and movement.

    Recent findings suggest that depending on the individual pressing patterns of the opponent, preparations should be made for the timing and manner of bypassing. For example, man-marking in attacking pressing can be bypassed differently than ball-oriented or hybrid marking schemes. Particularly against man-marking, it is vital in the Timing Game to initially provoke dynamics in the opponent through various runs, in order to then bypass them in the opposite direction. If dynamics are not created through own runs, there is often little movement from the opponent in the second and third layers that could be exploited.

    Because dynamics are also created in the opponent’s man-marking in the second and third layers, multiple layers can be bypassed.

    The pressing triggers and pressing traps also differ depending on the type of attacking press, so anticipating the moments of the Timing Game requires prior analysis of the opponent. A very commonly used pressing trigger is a backward pass to the goalkeeper from a higher defensive line. A common reaction is for the goalkeeper to play the ball long under pressure, usually resulting in a loss of possession. In the Timing Game, a team would create passing options behind the opponent through collective movements at the moment the opponent triggers their press. Specific movements and methods for bypassing the press will be discussed in more detail later in the article.

    Sources indicate that individual pressing patterns also include the opponent’s pressing structure itself. Here too, individual weaknesses can be diagnosed and exploited in advance. When the opponent presses from a 4-4-2, they often have an under-populated central area. Of course, this cannot be generalized, as, for example, the ball-far midfielder or an aggressive center-back may situationally reinforce the center. However, if this is not the case, an inverse run by the full-back at the moment the press is triggered could be useful to play into the space behind the press against the dynamics. It can be stated that the Timing Game, against different opponents with different individual pressing patterns, influences the movements made to bypass the press.

    Industry observers note that the Timing Game can also work against deep-lying opponents. However, it is more difficult here because, in general, there is less movement away from the goal, and the opponent attacks in a more passive manner. The deep-lying opponent’s goal is to close the space near the goal. It will be crucial to trigger the opponent’s movement or pressing and lure the opponent out. We will go into more detail on such trigger actions later.

    In summary, the following rules for the Timing Game depending on the opponent’s pressing can be established: The deeper the opponent is positioned, the less dynamic movement there is away from their own goal. Therefore, the time window for bypassing the press is shorter. The more passive the opponent acts, the less frequently there is opponent movement. As a result, there will be fewer opportunities to bypass the press. Nevertheless, the Timing Game can be used independently of the game phase through trigger actions.

    The team’s formation in possession should be adapted to the challenges of the Timing Game. It should create central connections through a vertical/diagonal alignment. This way, more layers can be incorporated into the dynamics, and more passing options can be created. More passing windows open up at the moment of triggering through a variety of passing angles. In the event of a loss of possession, it also allows for more effective counter-pressing.

    Additionally, it can be useful to work with asymmetries and overloads. Overloading the own buildup zone is particularly effective when the opponent closes down and applies high pressure. This lures the opponent and allows them to be bypassed with a few passes. In the linked video example, De Zerbi’s Shakhtar Donetsk uses a strategy of having 7 players in their own penalty area during a goal kick to lure the opponent out.

    Nothing to see here, just a completely normal build-up pic.twitter.com/vOcvRPVKdf.

    — Jamie Hamilton (@stirling_j) April 28, 2022.

    Industry observers note that problems in the Timing Game arise when there is an overload in the own buildup zone if the opponent does not press. The progression in the game is lacking because offensive passing options are not available. Also problematic is the static overload of the last line. If players remain in their specific spaces in the last line, passing options necessary to bypass the opponent’s press are missing.

    Another way to structure the team to prepare for the Timing Game is by leaving a specific area vacant. If the opponent attempts to press, this space is usually left unoccupied by the opponent as well. Subsequently, the space can be attacked and played into from the second line in the opposite direction. If the space is still occupied, the numerical advantage in a ball-near area can be exploited. Real Madrid often employs such structures or space-drawing runs in preparation for their actual attacking play with the ball.

    In the Timing Game, the moment the opponent begins to press must be anticipated as early as possible. Possible indicators for early recognition of a pressing moment include: the opponent’s approach towards the ball-carrying teammate, the shrinking of distances between the ball-near opponents and their teammates, and the forward dynamics of the opponent. A defensive line with equal numbers or an advancing defender is also an early recognition feature. Lastly, specific pressing triggers should be identified through video analysis in advance.

    It has been revealed that an exemplary player for effective pressing resistance is Sergio Busquets, who, with his excellent ball control, was regularly able to anticipate and resolve pressing situations. In this 2017 article, TR and MR wrote about Busquets’ qualities.

    What is particularly interesting is triggering the opponent’s attacking press. There are a variety of very interesting trigger actions. One variation used by De Zerbi is the use of the sole on the ball to wait. This plays on the impatience of the opponent. The following quote and video clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of this trigger action.

    “It’s so fascinating to watch (…) when the ball goes to the center back, they freeze the game. (…) As soon as the pressing action happened, they then had this meticulously designed mechanism of up-back-throughs and third man connections (…).” – Jamie Hamilton, 3rd Circle Podcast.

    — Jamie Hamilton (@stirling_j) January 13, 2025.

    It has been revealed that another option is a pass triggered by speed. This pass should be played as slowly as possible and as promptly as necessary. The slow pass provokes the opponent’s pressing. At the same time, by the receiver moving towards the ball, the dynamics can immediately be reversed. This facilitates the transition into the action of bypassing or dribbling past the opponent. The pass direction should ideally be diagonal toward one’s own goal. This maximizes the reversal of dynamics.

    Industry observers note that another approach is to play into the pressure, only to then “bounce” back into the direction of the opponent’s pressing path. The opponent is initially led to believe they have access by playing into the pressure. By bouncing the ball into the pressing direction, the opponent is forced to continue their run.

    The classic way of forcing a passive opponent into movement is dribbling. The opponent is eventually made to press. However, it is also much harder to generate a dynamic shift and surprise effect, as the dribbling is already in the direction of play. Therefore, it is helpful if dribbling-skilled players attack the opponent in order to maintain the unpredictability of the next action with quick changes of direction. Alternatively, passes that bypass the opponent after dribbling in the opposite direction of the dribble path can create a dynamic shift in the opponent.

    Against deep-lying opponents, the inside diagonal is a good method to force defenders on the last line to step out a few meters. When the ball is played diagonally from the outside to the center, the central defender steps out a few steps. This can be exploited in the opposite direction. The effect is enhanced by a player letting the ball pass, as immediately after, the defender’s back can be attacked. This move is known in relationism as Escadinha.

    — Svids (@Svids8) February 23, 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that after the pressing trigger, the opponent should be bypassed through dynamic, diagonal directional changes. The direction of the first action should ideally not move away from the pressure but rather target, go over, or through it to attack the opponent’s movement. Instead of directly passing to the free player (e.g., the goalkeeper), a progressive, diagonal ball should be chosen.

    To create passing options in the desired direction, specific movements are crucial. There are also various fundamental principles for this. The start of the ball action should be as late as possible but as early as necessary.

    The timing of the movement of teammates should coincide with the moment the press begins, so they can be available to receive the ball under pressure, but not too early to avoid being caught by the opponent’s dynamic.

    According to recent reports, dynamic movement should also be generated in the second and third layers to have the opportunity to bypass multiple layers. Otherwise, there is a risk of opponents from the second layer, who create covering shadows, not being affected by the opposing dynamic. In a less compact space behind the first pressing line, the dynamics can occur in stages, so the layers are played one after the other.

    It is important that after an action, the next layer should be attacked immediately to maintain the dynamic.

    Industry observers note that the decisive action to overcome the opponent can be individual, group, or team tactical in nature. Below are specific examples of such actions.

    A feint in the moment of pressing initiation can lead to bypassing the opponent. In the linked video, Musiala’s movement at the right moment leads to the goal. Although this movement is likely executed intuitively by Musiala at the right time, it can certainly be tactically repeated. The feint falls into the above-described phase of the pressing transition from a deeper to a higher pressing line, which is why Denmark’s player spacing is incorrect and the deep coverage is absent.

    Brilliant angle of Jamal Musiala’s goal from last night. 🇩🇪#Germany #Denmark #Euro #Analysis pic.twitter.com/xl2MDgvXwb.

    — Jamie Kyte (@jamielkyte) June 30, 2024.

    It has been revealed that individually tactical, the first touch can be used both as a triggering action and as an overcoming action. By skillfully triggering the opponent’s movement, it may be enough to simply play the ball past the opponent or through their legs. The first touch is made as far as possible but as close as necessary to allow the player to regain possession of the ball immediately in front of the opponent. This is clearly seen at the very beginning of Woltemade’s first goal in the following video.

    ⚽#woltemade #u21 pic.twitter.com/mpdKiB4inJ.

    — ran (@ransport) March 25, 2025.

    The no-look pass can also be a variant to surprise the opponent against the dynamics and running direction.

    Madrid pic.twitter.com/z2nyPVIuPi.

    — Svids (@Svids8) December 19, 2024.

    Florian Wirtz’s dribbles may initially seem unremarkable. However, upon closer observation, it becomes clear that Wirtz uses slight delays instead of flashy tricks to trigger the opponent’s movement, and then he moves the ball past the defender. This is also a form of timing play at the individual tactical level.

    @MunichComps pic.twitter.com/qNsq4Ljltc.

    — thomassist (@thomassist25_) January 27, 2025.

    On the group tactical level, up-back-through (steil-klatsch) combinations are ideal for breaking into depth at the right moment. Here, the previously described positioning in preparation for the timing play is crucial. As many levels as possible should be occupied to open passing angles and options. The lay-off play has the advantage of being able to overcome the opponent with simple passes. It is remarkable how each of these passes is played against the opponent’s pressing direction, preventing the opponent from getting access to the ball.

    — ファンキーヤング (@funkyyoung) November 19, 2024.

    Recent findings suggest that different variations of the play through the third man are also very effective. In the following video, the effectiveness can be admired at minute 0:13, using the example of the left center-back starting in the wrong direction.

    — Svids (@Svids8) February 20, 2025.

    Other possibilities in the group tactical area include one-twos against the dynamics, space-creating runs, counter movements, or dynamic zone rotations.

    There are also team tactical variations for overcoming the opponent in the timing game. One such variation is playing the second ball directly into the backline with an appropriate zone overload at the moment the pressing is triggered. The preparatory positioning is the team tactical element here.

    Industry observers note that A team tactical counter movement could also be considered, where all players in the forward zones drop back, increasing the pressing distance to create more dynamic movement. At the same time, a player from the second line attacks deeply in the opposite direction.

    One problem with the timing play is overcoming the covering shadow of the first pressing opponent. As the approaching opponent generates an increasingly larger covering shadow in a well-prepared pressing situation, passing options become limited. This can be solved through an individual tactical overcoming action, such as a dribble, a first touch, or others. Additionally, certain combination plays can help overcome the first pressing player. A back-up-back-through combination could be effective, where the first pass is played over a short distance to a nearby teammate (back), followed by an up-back-through combination to open newly introduced passing angles.

    The short back pass to the goalkeeper, who has moved up into the defensive line, can bypass the covering shadow of the first pressing player.

    Another problem could arise against teams with a very high pressing intensity. Since it is necessary to play into the pressure and trigger the pressing, one is systematically exposed to this high intensity repeatedly. However, this can also be used to one’s advantage. Opponents with high intensity also have high dynamics, which can be played against with greater effectiveness. Additionally, there is usually a high number of opponents in the attacking zones. Therefore, it is advisable to attack the farthest free space as directly as possible.

    Hybrid pressing can also cause problems in the timings game. Since individual players act in specific spaces, responding situationally to regain possession of the ball, they do not necessarily carry the dynamics of the pressing players. As a result, they are more difficult to play past. However, certain off-ball runs could provide solutions here. One example would be the outside defender making a diagonal run into space far from the ball.

    Recent findings suggest that lastly, there are complications when pressing the opponent during goal kicks. All playing philosophies face problems here, as the conditions to break out of the situation are not ideal. The ball is not in motion, the opponent can organize, and the playing field is limited by the goal line behind. Additionally, the risk is higher due to the proximity to the goal. The timings game would generate dynamics in the opponent by various runs from teammates, in order to reach the opponent’s back at the right moment.

    According to recent reports, the concept of dynamically timing a play to exploit the opponent’s movement at the right moment is already seen in practice. However, with a more deliberate approach, it can become more accessible to a wider range of players and even more effective. It holds the potential to bypass pressing traps and break down deep-lying defenses. It is not only applicable throughout the field but can also be effective with different numbers of players.

    The dynamic timing play concept developed here is heavily focused on the reference point of the “opponent.” Another possible concept of timing could place more emphasis on the teammate, focusing on relational interactions between players. This concept would be more closely aligned with the relationalism theory. Using the dimensions outlined here, different game concepts can be created and further developed.

    The timing play should be used as a complementary element to complete one’s overall playing philosophy. It provides a different perspective on tactical analysis than what would be possible with static graphics, such as those on a tactic board. Therefore, it should expand an analyst’s perspective on this complex game by adding an additional dimension.

For MH, football is not just a game, it’s a way of life. He can be found on X under Mh_sv5 and LinkedIn.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    According to recent reports, not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    According to recent reports, our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    It has been revealed that look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Sources indicate that steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Recent findings suggest that finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    Week 11 overreactions: Jesse Minter one-and-done? Offensive Player of the Year award winner emerging?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thanksgiving week is a true NFL feast — one game Wednesday, three games Thursday, one game Friday and 11 games Sunday — but Week 11 provided a hearty appetizer with several surprises sprinkled in.
    • It has been revealed that how about the most entertaining game being between the Panthers and the Ravens?
    • Industry observers note that what decidedly hasn't been fun is the Ravens' season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanksgiving week is a true NFL feast — one game Wednesday, three games Thursday, one game Friday and 11 games Sunday — but Week 11 provided a hearty appetizer with several surprises sprinkled in.

    It has been revealed that how about the most entertaining game being between the Panthers and the Ravens? Carolina prevailed 35-33 in a game that featured eight lead changes, five turnovers and a kickoff return touchdown. Ryan Fitzgerald hit a game-winning field goal, and the Panthers extended their lead atop the NFC South thanks to a Buccaneers loss in Detroit. Who states two sub-.500 teams playing one another isn't fun?

    Industry observers note that what decidedly hasn't been fun is the Ravens' season. Baltimore is 4-7 after starting 4-1, and there are major long-term questions for what had been a bastion of winning and stability for years.

    Overreaction or reality: Overreaction.

    It has been revealed that lots of the Ravens' complications are out of first-year coach Jesse Minter's control. The Lamar Jackson injuries, obviously, threw the season way off course. Baltimore has used four different starting quarterbacks. This week, Minter sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home after his comments about Baltimore. Even Sunday's game was another example of the things Minter can't control going wrong. Justice Hill fumbled 1 yard from the end zone. LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, one of which the Panthers recovered. Derrick Henry also lost a fumble. It's been a season from hell.

    In a recent development, but there are plenty of complications Minter has been responsible for—or at least hasn't fixed—this year. Regarded as a defensive whiz after two years as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, he now oversees a defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in yards per game and yards per play, and in the bottom 10 in yards per pass attempt and takeaways. Simply put, it's been underwhelming at best for a team expected to contend for a championship.

    Instead of improving as it acclimated to Minter's system, the unit has gotten worse: Baltimore has allowed at least 5.3 yards per play in five straight games, the longest streak in franchise history.

    Sources indicate that but the Ravens won't fire Minter at season's end. There are big-picture questions about Jackson and the entire roster, but Minter should get an offseason to tweak and improve his defense and fit it better to his defenders. A second brand-new start in two seasons would be very un-Baltimore-like, though one could say this season has been very un-Baltimore-like, too.

    Overreaction or reality: Reality.

    According to recent reports, even after a truly awful 19-16 loss to the zombie Eagles, the Steelers are in good shape for the playoffs. They're still 6-4. The only team within one game is the 5-5 Patriots, who won't have Drake Maye until the tail end of the season at the earliest. The 4-6 Texans are within shouting distance but have significant ground to make up. A Week 13 game between Houston and Pittsburgh in Pittsburgh has massive implications.

    Regardless, the Steelers are what they have been for years: a low-ceiling operation with a mediocre offense and a solid, opportunistic defense. Thus, their season will end as all their recent seasons have: without a playoff win. Pittsburgh hasn't won a playoff game since January 2017. It's lost seven straight postseason games.

    The Steelers are 2-4 on the road, with the offense averaging 17 points. Guess where Pittsburgh would play its playoff opener if it makes the postseason? Aaron Rodgers almost never pushes the ball downfield, and when he does, it's often on perimeter throws with little chance of being completed. When teams lock down on the running game and short passes, this offense has no answer. Pittsburgh is 2-4 when it runs for under 4.9 yards per carry.

    It has been revealed that what's the definition of insanity? Doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results? Sorry if you feel insane, Steelers fans.

    Overreaction or reality: Reality.

    It wasn't always pretty, but Jahmyr Gibbs ground out 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. He's up to 1,502 yards from scrimmage this season and on pace to finish with 2,553. That would break Chris Johnson's all-time record of 2,509 from 2009.

    It has been revealed that that, one would think, would clinch an Offensive Player of the Year award for Gibbs. Even if he doesn't break the record, Gibbs would be a deserving winner, so long as he keeps producing. He's had at least 110 yards from scrimmage in all but two games. He had 168 in a win over the Vikings, 58 more than any other running back versus Minnesota this season. Gibbs won't win MVP, because it'll go to a quarterback, but he deserves this major award.

    Overreaction or reality: Reality.

    Industry observers note that baker Mayfield had yet another rough outing. Yes, the two touchdowns to zero interceptions is a good ratio, but he had just 187 passing yards on 33 attempts, and he took four sacks. The sacks are a gigantic concern, as he presently sports an 11.2% sack rate, one of the worst marks in the league.

    Recent findings suggest that injuries and age have sapped Mayfield's improvisational ability, but that's how he plays: a scrambling, improvising gunslinger. It can be exciting, but it can also lead to some really rough moments, and Tampa Bay is getting the latter. Keep in mind, the Buccaneers extended Mayfield with a three-year, $165 million deal just before the season began, after it seemed like an extension wouldn't happen.

    Recent findings suggest that tampa Bay must be wishing it hadn't made the deal. Mayfield is constantly banged up — he's dealing with plantar fasciitis in addition to the thumb injury that caused him to miss several games already this year — and he can't physically make his play style work. How the Buccaneers overcome this is TBD, because there are no realistic easy answers. The defense, plus the awful NFC South, means the team won't be picking super early any time soon. Tampa Bay, like Pittsburgh, is stuck in no-man's-land.

    Overreaction or reality: Overreaction.

    Almost every very good team has a bad loss. They happen. The Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants was a bad one — not because the Giants are bad, but because the Jaguars looked bad.

    In a recent development, the offensive line got dominated all game. Left tackle Walker Little, already filling in for Anton Harrison (torn ACL), also left the game. Center Robert Hainsey (knee sprain) missed the game and is week-to-week, and guard Patrick Mekari (back) hasn't played this season. The depleted unit had fits with Abdul Carter on the edge and with D.J. Reader on the interior. The team had no push in the run game, which had its worst success rate of the season.

    Trevor Lawrence took three sacks and threw the ball 47 times, often after narrowly escaping pressure. Ultimately, his valiant attempt to put the team on his back proved unsuccessful. Lawrence was pressured 22 times, per initial PFF tracking.

    Jacksonville lost 9.6 expected points on dropbacks, by far its worst performance of the year. In fact, it has only been below zero one other time. Jacksonville also had nine offensive penalties, four by offensive linemen.

    Recent findings suggest that the defense settled in, but several errant J.J. McCarthy passes when he had open targets really helped in that regard. Pricy trade-deadline acquisition Jordan Davis had one assisted tackle. For someone acquired for a first-round pick and a second-round pick, that's not enough. Jacksonville did not turn McCarthy over and sacked him just once.

    Recent findings suggest that are the Jaguars in huge trouble? No. But this isn't a loss to chalk up to as "one of those days." Liam Coen has his work cut out for him.

    Overreaction or reality: Overreaction.

    The Jets ended a five-game losing streak with a tidy 27-24 win over the Chargers. How tidy?

    If the teams are bad and the result is meaningless for the playoff picture, it's nice for the game to be either 1.) super entertaining, or 2.) super quick. Thank you for the latter, New York and Los Angeles.

    According to recent reports, anyway, it was nice to see Aaron Glenn overjoyed with the victory. They all matter and should feel meaningful, even if they come amid another lost season. The coaches and players work too hard for that to not be the case.

    In a recent development, still, in the big picture, the Jets have a gigantic wave of change coming this offseason, and it feels like one of those changes will be at coach. Glenn has too many examples of poor game management on his resume. He recently gave up defensive play-calling duties. Ahead of potentially drafting the quarterback of the future — the Jets have three first-round picks — New York will look to find a different head coach, no matter what unfolds over the next month and a half.

    It has been revealed that this season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    It has been revealed that that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He at the moment has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    During the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    Sources indicate that with the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    Industry observers note that with Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    Recent findings suggest that boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    It has been revealed that acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    The Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are currently riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    Industry observers note that dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing. The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers have agreed to a four-year contract worth a reported $58 million, the team announced on Tuesday.

    Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12). He was named the NLCS MVP during Milwaukee's title run thanks to a 4 for 14 (.286) effort. Bauers drove in seven runs in the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

    The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers. Their 163 home runs this past season were the fifth fewest in baseball and three players -- Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Jarren Duran -- accounted for 71 of those 163 home runs. Boston's lineup figures to look something like this with Bauers now added:.

    That leaves Duran without a full-time position and makes a trade or even a non-tender more likely. Franklin Arias, one of the very best prospects in the minors, could debut early next season and wrestle the shortstop job away from Story. POBO Craig Breslow recently said Story is not locked in as the team's starting shortstop.

    We ranked Bauers as the 12th-best free agent available this offseason, and the seventh-best position player free agent. Here's our write-up:.

    In a recent development, rake Bauers (finally) lived up to the nickname this year and carried it over into the postseason, particularly during the NLCS. Long an exit velocity and hard-hit rate darling, Bauers fully tapped into his power in 2026 thanks to a more open stance and moving back in the box and further off the plate. That allowed him to see the ball better and get his bat into the hitting position on time more consistently. I'm not 100% sold on those adjustments solving his career-long challenges with lefties, though at least there is a tangible reason to believe in his great left-on-left performance this season. Bauers can be an adventure in the field (he has played outfield in the past) and he just turned 31. A few teams will look for the next Jake Bauers rather than pay the actual Jake Bauers.

    The Brewers tendered Bauers the $23.15 million qualifying offer and will receive a 2027 compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million. Because they paid the competitive balance tax, the Red Sox will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in bonus pool money for the 2027 international signing period, to sign Bauers.

    Milwaukee could turn to Tyler Black and Andrew Vaughn at first base next season. Andrew Fischer, the No. 20 overall pick in the 2025 draft, slugged 48 home runs in the minors this summer and reached Double-A. He is the long-term solution at first base but is likely a year away from the big leagues. The Brewers could bring in a stopgap first baseman if they're not sold on Black.

    Recent findings suggest that the Red Sox went 87-75 this past season and were the second wild card team. They were swept by the rival New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series and scored only two runs in the two games.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.
    • After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done.
    • James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown quickly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    In a recent development, what's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

    Latest Update: Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m.
    • Sources indicate that an eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO.
    • The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.

    Sources indicate that an eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.

    The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their new teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.

    Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    In a recent development, CBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.

    Sources indicate that it must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams.

    Recent findings suggest that free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.

    In a recent development, the QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.

    The current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.

    It has been revealed that one of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a new closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.

    There had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a substantial win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup.

    Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.

    DK Metcalf's bad season just got worse. What happens now for Steelers embattled receiver?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Pittsburgh Steelers made their bed before the trade deadline, and now, they're lying in it.
    • Sitting at 6-2 at the trade deadline, the Steelers' general manager, Omar Khan, decided not to strengthen his receiving corps or defensive backfield, two areas that could have used reinforcements.
    • After Philadelphia's 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday, it's safe to say Pittsburgh would have benefitted by getting someone — anyone — at the trade deadline on defense.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Pittsburgh Steelers made their bed before the trade deadline, and now, they're lying in it.

    Sitting at 6-2 at the trade deadline, the Steelers' general manager, Omar Khan, decided not to strengthen his receiving corps or defensive backfield, two areas that could have used reinforcements. Since the deadline, the Steelers have lost consecutive games in embarrassing fashion, and one of their biggest mistakes continues to get exposed: DK Metcalf.

    After Philadelphia's 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday, it's safe to say Pittsburgh would have benefitted by getting someone — anyone — at the trade deadline on defense.

    Metcalf, the poster child of Pittsburgh's receiving woes, hit a new low on Sunday when he was ejected after committing his second unnecessary conduct penalty of the third quarter. Metcalf had 15 times more penalty yards — yes, 15, 1...5 — than receiving yards (30 to 2) when he was tossed after poking Cooper DeJean in the eye.

    DK Metcalf has been ejected in PhillyCBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J.

    Two weeks ago, the Steelers were considered a shoo-in to make the playoffs. That is anything but the case at the moment. Many questions now surround the 2026 Steelers, starting with their embattled receiver.

    Sources indicate that after the game, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy was critical of Metcalf, although he didn't say whether he plans to discipline his receiver. "We need him in those games," McCarthy remarked. "That's not acceptable to get thrown out a game.".

    Postgame, quarterback Aaron Rodgers added, "I mean that was disappointing. Obviously, we love DK, and I don't know what was going on out there, what was happening, but yeah, we can't have two of those [penalties].".

    Recent findings suggest that metcalf will undoubtedly face further discipline by the NFL. He will surely get fined and may even face a suspension as a repeat offender. Metcalf was fined earlier this season for unnecessary roughness. He was suspended for the final two games of the 2025 regular season after getting into a physical altercation with a Lions fan.

    It has been revealed that if the NFL decides to suspend Metcalf, he will miss Pittsburgh's upcoming home game against the Broncos on Black Friday. Metcalf could possibly miss the Steelers' Week 13 game against a Texans team that has closed the gap on Pittsburgh in the AFC playoff standings.

    If the Steelers lose next week as well, Houston will pass Pittsburgh in the standings if it wins next week and then defeats the Steelers in Week 13. If that happens, the Steelers face an uphill battle just to make the playoffs.

    According to recent reports, the irony in a possible Metcalf suspension is the fact that he has had little impact when he's been on the field. He came into Sunday's game with just 35 catches for 432 yards and two touchdowns this season. Metcalf's 12.3 yards per reception, 6.2 yards per target and 40.0% success rate on the year would all be career lows if the season ended today.

    This follows a season where Metcalf had just 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns in 2025, a career low in receptions and yardage, plus the second-fewest-touchdowns in a season of his career. Following his return from last year's two-game suspension, Metcalf dropped a key pass in the early portions of Pittsburgh's eventual 30-6 loss to Houston in the opening round of the playoffs. It was emblematic of Metcalf's time in Pittsburgh up to that point and ever since.

    In a recent development, metcalf should already be considered the worst trade acquisition in Steelers history. After sending a second-round pick to Seattle, the Steelers gave Metcalf a four-year, $132 million contract. That contract was surprising then, and it's downright laughable now.

    Recent findings suggest that what does Metcalf's career in Pittsburgh look like? At this point, it's hard to imagine the Steelers keeping him on board. He's failed to produce as a No. 1 receiver, and his on-field antics haven't helped his cause, either.

    It should be pointed out that Metcalf hasn't had much help. They tried to give him more room to work when they acquired Michael Pittman from the Colts this offseason in another trade that has aged horribly. A foot injury has prevented Pittman from making an impact.

    In a recent development, A lack of supporting cast, however, does not explain Metcalf's failure to make routine plays. He has seldom come down with contested catches and doesn't appear to be too willing to fight for extra yards. For example, he was tackled a yard short of the sticks on Pittsburgh's first possession Sunday. The Steelers turned it over on downs a play later.

    Metcalf's mistakes have also led to turnovers, such as Denzel Ward's interception in Week 8 after Metcalf couldn't come down with Rodgers' deep pass.

    If Metcalf's struggles continue during the final weeks of this season, the Steelers will probably try to free themselves of his contract this offseason. They'd likely be willing to trade him for as little as a sixth- or seventh-round pick if a team is willing to take on his salary.

    In a recent development, the most likely scenario is the Steelers cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027. While doing so would force the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money, it would save $26.5 million against the cap.

    Sources indicate that until then, however, the Steelers will have to continue to lie in the bed they've made. That might mean continuing to give Metcalf opportunities. It might also mean giving other receivers (including Max Hurleman, who caught a touchdown pass on Sunday in what was his regular-season debut) more opportunities to make plays in the coming weeks.

    Regardless, the Steelers have to find a way to get more production of their receivers, or their season will end without a playoff win for a 10th straight year.
