    • The hot stove is starting to heat up.
    • Sources indicate that we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up.
    • The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

    Sources indicate that we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

    The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

    Industry observers note that fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a substantial dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

    The Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

    It has been revealed that skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are said to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

    Star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

    Seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

    According to recent reports, on Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

    San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

    Recent findings suggest that after signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow mentioned it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

    In a recent development, breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster problems remaining this offseason.

    Free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

    Although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

    The Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

    Recent findings suggest that still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

    Sources indicate that veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

    Industry observers note that pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.

    Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • According to recent reports, hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Latest Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams unveiled the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    According to recent reports, hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He stated at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    It has been revealed that after trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Newly introduced Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Latest Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    Recent findings suggest that for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a upcoming era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    According to recent reports, goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Recent findings suggest that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Fresh Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    It has been revealed that hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Industry observers note that although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    Sources indicate that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    According to recent reports, let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    That mentioned, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    According to recent reports, with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his fresh team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    Sources indicate that if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    It has been revealed that the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota.
    • Industry observers note that skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray!
    • Gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday unveiled they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the Fresh York Post.

    Industry observers note that skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

    Gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

    Sources indicate that CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

    Gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, big movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

    Gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

    Recent findings suggest that the Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that when Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards went down after four games, I ranked it as the biggest injury blow any team has suffered this season, which was saying a lot given all the injuries we've seen.
    • In a recent development, how are they doing it?
    • And by elite, we mean the best in the league.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that when Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards went down after four games, I ranked it as the biggest injury blow any team has suffered this season, which was saying a lot given all the injuries we've seen. As it turned out, Oklahoma City's barrage of injuries, Kawhi Leonard in Toronto, Tyrese Haliburton in Indiana, Jaren Jackson Jr. in Utah, Paolo Banchero in Orlando, and now Stephen Curry with the Warriors have all turned out to be significantly more debilitating as Minnesota has gone 8-3 without Edwards.

    In a recent development, how are they doing it? Let's take a look.

    And by elite, we mean the best in the league. Minnesota is surrendering just 104 points per 100 possessions. Give Rudy Gobert his flowers, man. The Wolves' defensive rating drops to 97 points per 100 when he's on the court, while rising to 108.6 when he sits. That mentioned, the Wolves have defenders everywhere you look and they are seriously tied together.

    It has been revealed that with their four regular starters on the floor (LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, Jonathan Kuminga and Gobert), Minnesota is registering a 92.0 defensive rating with a plus-20.5 net rating. But even when they go smaller and swap in Ayo Dosunmu for Gobert with the other three, the rating stays at 94.2 with a plus-16.2 net.

    According to recent reports, no matter the combination, if four of those five guys are on the court, the defense is no worse than 96.0. It's super impressive stuff, and so much for the idea that Ball is a defensive liability. Speaking of Ball ...

    According to recent reports, the LaMelo effect is being felt in two places: Minnesota, of course, but also Charlotte, where the offense has plummeted from a 123.3 rating with Ball on the court last year to a league-worst 103.1 this season. Being down Kon Knueppel doesn't help, but it's night and day watching this unit try to generate clean looks without Ball's creation and passing.

    Meanwhile, the Wolves are flying. The defense is carrying the day and we're going to get to some of the guys carrying more impressive statistical weight than Ball, at least relatively, but watch this team play and try to argue his impact isn't all over the floor. He won the game for Minnesota on Tuesday with two defensive plays over the closing seconds.

    Sources indicate that laMelo wins the game with back to back defensive plays! Who would have thought? 👀 pic.twitter.com/v9xYpR7eZu.

    Sources indicate that of course, his impact is felt most offensively. The pace. Energy. All of Minnesota's shooting percentages go up with Ball on the court, as they did last season in Charlotte, and that's not because of Ball's own shooting. He's only making 41.8% of his own shots, after all. It's his passing, his flow. As fancy as it is, it's fundamental in its contagious, force-multiplying impact.

    It has been revealed that the bottom line is this: Over his last 53 games between Charlotte and Minnesota, Ball has gone 39-14. That's the pace of a 60-win team. He's an agent of chaos, fine. It can look out of control. He still chucks up the playground shots, often off one foot and from barely inside the boundary. But we all wondered what it would look like when he was playing for a team with real stakes. Is he a winner? Or are his stats empty? Honestly, he's not even that impressive of a stats guy so far. He's just a winner.

    It has been revealed that the Wolves can deploy uncompromised lineups up and down their roster, meaning they don't have to decide between offense and defense. All their guys do both. They also have multiple offensive weapons even without Edwards, which is why Ball isn't having to carry a bigger scoring burden than he's equipped to handle, at least efficiently.

    According to recent reports, terrence Shannon Jr. put up 34 off the bench in a win over Portland on Monday. The next night, Dosunmu and McDaniels, who are playing at legit All-Star levels, combined for 52 with nine 3-pointers. Kuminga is giving them 12.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, almost three assists and a steal over 30 minutes per game.

    According to recent reports, other than Gobert, Jaylen Clark is really the only truly offensively limited guy, but for the minutes he gets, he is one hell of a defender. You do not want this man guarding you. You do not want anything to do with this team overall.

    They came out of the gate looking incredible with Edwards and Ball looking like basketball brothers. It seemed like that was going to die out when Edwards got hurt. It hasn't.

    When Edwards gets back, this Timberwolves team has the look of a legitimate contender.
